Design problem: Design a car-mounted bicycle rack that addresses the following needs: (1) Easy mounting of the bicycle, (2) Easy mounting of the rack, (3) Cannot harm bike or car, and (4) Must be versatile for all bikes and cars.

Below is an example of a present day bike rack. The bicycle is set in the rails and the vinyl coated hook is attached to the seat tube of the bike, and then the hook is tightened down by hand with a wing nut. One should note the difficulty of mounting the middle bikes on the rack.

Please study the problem and this example. You will be asked to come up with your own designs later.

Idea generation

Early in a design process, designers use divergent thinking: coming up with many different possible solutions to a problem before choosing one to develop. The goal at this stage is to create multiple, diverse concepts.

In the parts that follow:

  • Generate varied, alternative concepts.
  • Sketch your concepts without worrying about your drawing skills. Rough sketches are fine.
  • Draw and describe each concept on its own concept sheet. Use Save and start a new concept to begin the next one. Sheets are numbered for you, and you can go back to edit any sheet using the Go to list above it.

Individual brainstorming

Brainstorming is a method for generating ideas. When brainstorming on your own:

  1. Postpone and withhold your judgment of ideas.
  2. Encourage wild and exaggerated ideas.
  3. Quantity counts at this stage, not quality.
  4. Build consecutively on your ideas.
  5. Every idea has equal worth.

Next, you will practice brainstorming on a practice problem for a few minutes.

trials.description: It's a v shaped piece, which can seat the tire of a bicycle

This designs has been inspired by US busses, which have frontal bike racks, designed to be for quick and easy use. The design has a rail where the wheels of the bike will rest in, and two spring tensioned arms that can clamp on both the front and back wheel. This will be sufficient to keep the bike on tightly.
The bike will be placed on a slightly larger rack, which will keep it upright. Then 2 ratchets will clamp down each will, so that it will be tightly fastened to the rack.

This will be a symilair kind of system explained at the start, where you will have a fixed bar that would be clamped down to the frame of the bicycle, but this would bicycle rack would be mounted on a tow hitch behind the car. This would make for easier mounting of both the bicycle and the rack itselfs.

This design has two upstanding arms, with a universal seating the frame of a bicycle. The bycicle can be placed on top of the seats and can be straped down with a ratchet system. This can make for easier mounting of the bike and make it more universal for all kinds of different bicycles.
